title: A Deadline for the Protocol
premise: Edmund Dravenmoor, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Consulate—an embassy that exists on no map—receives a debt notice from a stranger claiming he once saved her life. He never did, but the favor is real: she hands him proof that a staged 'accident' will destroy a border checkpoint during shift change, killing hundreds and igniting a war his employers quietly want. Hunted by both the plotters and his own handlers, Edmund must decide whether he is the man in the forged memory or someone better, racing to expose the protocol before the clocks at Vellmark Crossing align. In the end he burns his own legend to stop the attack, inheriting not power but its consequences.
about_author: W. M. Voss is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent six years drafting contingency plans for organizations that preferred to remain unnamed. They write thrillers about paperwork, borders, and the people who fall through both.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag by the Door
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A routine errand—burning a diplomat's affair—establishes his cold competence and the polished lie of his life. He notices his go-bag is packed but can't remember packing it. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: A woman named Ilse Varga corners him in a tram station, thanking him for saving her life in Rijeka—a rescue that never happened. She leaves an envelope with photographs and a timestamp. Emotional beat: vertigo; his identity has been edited without his consent.

chapters.title: The Meridian Consulate
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He reports the contact to his handler, Corvane, who dismisses it too quickly. Edmund realizes the consulate already knows about Vellmark Crossing. Emotional beat: the first crack in loyalty.

chapters.title: Photographs of a Man Who Isn't Him
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. She studies the photos: Edmund at the checkpoint, wearing his face, three weeks before she ever met him. Someone built a version of him inside the plot. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Shift Change at 04:40
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He pulls the checkpoint rosters and finds the attack window buried in a maintenance schedule signed with his own authorization code. Emotional beat: betrayal turning personal.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. A man called Ferro follows her, polite and patient, asking only that she 'return what was borrowed.' She realizes the favor was bait designed to reel in Edmund. Emotional beat: hunted but unbroken.

chapters.title: Corvane's Kindness
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. His handler offers him extraction and a new name—the inheritance every fixer dreams of—if he lets the checkpoint fall. The offer reveals the consulate's complicity. Emotional beat: temptation with rot underneath.

chapters.title: Rijeka, Reconstructed
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Edmund and Ilse piece together the fabricated rescue: a real operation where a double wore his face and let a family die. The forgery was built from a true failure. Emotional beat: grief as evidence.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Holed up with Ilse, they count assets: one stolen drive, forty hours, no allies. He teaches her how a fixer thinks; she teaches him what the dead were owed. Emotional beat: wary trust becoming partnership.

chapters.title: The Drive That Lies
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The stolen drive contains the attack plan—and a second protocol listing names to be blamed afterward. Edmund's is first. Emotional beat: clarity; there is no version of this where he survives by obeying.

chapters.title: Ferro's Offer
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Ferro captures him briefly, not to kill him but to recruit him: the plotters are ex-consulate, men who inherited the machine and resent serving it. Power as dynasty. Emotional beat: horror at recognizing his own future.

chapters.title: Escape by Paperwork
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. She springs Edmund using forged transit orders—his own tradecraft turned back on his captors. Emotional beat: triumph laced with fear; she is becoming what she's fighting.

chapters.title: What Corvane Inherited
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He confronts Corvane, learning the consulate's founding charter treats atrocities as line items passed down like property. Corvane genuinely believes he's sparing Edmund. Emotional beat: pity for a man fully corrupted.

chapters.title: The Widow of Vellmark
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. They find the last living witness of the original Rijeka op, who confirms the double existed—and that Ilse's 'rescue' was staged to compromise whoever answered it. Emotional beat: fury transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Burning the Legend
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. To move freely he must erase himself: he torches his covers, accounts, and aliases, mailing fragments to journalists as insurance. Emotional beat: liberation in self-destruction.

chapters.title: Countdown Logistics
chapters.summary: Dual POV. With eighteen hours left, they map the checkpoint: which guards, which generator, which truck carrying the charge disguised as road salt. Emotional beat: taut focus, love acknowledged in glances, never words.

chapters.title: The Insider's Face
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The plot's inside man is his double—the man with his face. To stop the attack he must become indistinguishable from his own forgery. Emotional beat: identity as weapon and wound.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Dual POV. At 04:15 they infiltrate the checkpoint; Ilse cuts the detonation link while Edmund walks into the control room wearing his own stolen face. Emotional beat: terror held in perfect stillness.

chapters.title: A Deadline for the Protocol
chapters.summary: Climax. Edmund's POV. He faces the double and Ferro; the detonation fails, Ferro dies by his own protocol's fail-safe, and Edmund chooses arrest over escape to force public testimony. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship.

chapters.title: Testimony Without a Name
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Edmund, in custody, gives everything under a name that isn't his; the consulate disavows him, but the record now exists outside their walls. Emotional beat: costly vindication.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Released when the scandal breaks, he inherits nothing but the truth—and Ilse's real gratitude, the favor finally earned retroactively. Emotional beat: quiet peace after ruin.

chapters.title: The Bag Left Behind
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Ilse's POV. She finds Edmund's go-bag abandoned at a tram station, unpacked deliberately, a note inside: 'Some debts you pay forward.' Somewhere, a new stranger is being handed a favor that never happened. Emotional beat: hope shadowed by the cycle continuing.
